facts.text: GDR2Env derives from gym.Env and models a simple 1D point-mass system whose state is position and velocity and whose action is one force value
The environment advertises the human render mode with render_fps 20
The constructor sets max_steps to 1000 and dt to 0.05
The observation space is Box([-1.0, -5.0], [1.0, 5.0], dtype=float32) over position and velocity
The action space is Box(low=-1.0, high=1.0, shape=(1,), dtype=float32), one force value
The constructor creates a Docker network named gdr2-network, the simulation-container and dynamics-container from gdr2-image:latest, and a ZeroMQ REQ socket to 10.42.0.20:5555
reset sends the special control value 9999.0 over ZeroMQ, unpacks a ddii position/velocity/time reply, stores position and velocity and resets step_count
step sends the force over ZeroMQ, unpacks the same ddii position/velocity/time reply and stores position and velocity
A step returns reward -abs(position), terminated false, truncated when step_count reaches max_steps, and (observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info)
close stops the simulation and dynamics containers, removes the network and closes the ZeroMQ socket and context
_get_obs returns the float32 array [position, velocity] and _get_info returns position and velocity
test.py registers GDR2Env-v0 with entry_point GDR2Env and creates the environment with render_mode human
The declared runtime requires Python ^3.13 with numpy, gymnasium, docker and pyzmq
The README describes GDR2 as a multi-container Docker/Gazebo/ROS2 app wrapped in gymnasium, installed with pip install -e . and exercised with test.py --mode step, speed or learn
DynamicsNode computes dt as 1.0 / rate and seeds NumPy to 42 once at construction
The DynamicsNode command line defaults rate to 50 Hz
The simulation launch runs the dynamics node with --rate 20
The world SDF fixes max_step_size to 0.050 s and real_time_factor to 0.0
The dynamics reset branch triggers within 0.1 of control input 9999.0, draws position uniformly from -0.8 to 0.8 and sets velocity to 0
The dynamics update integrates velocity += control_input * dt, multiplies velocity by 0.99, integrates position += velocity * dt, clips position to [-1, 1] and multiplies velocity by -0.5 at a wall
The Python ZeroMQ bridge requests one Gazebo multi-step per request with a 1 s service timeout, then waits up to 2.0 s for a new /state and packs the reply as ddii

determinism.notes: the fake reseeds a Python random.Random from reset(seed), and cap.world.seed.v1 selects the seed of the next reset, so one seed repeats the fake's trajectory; the live dynamics node seeds NumPy to 42 once at construction and its reset branch ignores the Gymnasium seed, so a container run repeats only while that node process keeps its RNG sequence

gaps: the fake reproduces only the dynamics node's one-dimensional Euler update; there is no Docker, ZeroMQ, ROS 2, Gazebo, C++/Python bridge, /state round trip or rendering, and no rigid-body, contact, actuator, sensor or noise dynamics

the live dynamics node seeds NumPy to 42 once at startup and ignores the Gymnasium reset seed, while the fake reseeds from reset(seed); one seed therefore repeats in the fake and is not guaranteed to repeat against a live container

no wall-clock pacing: real_time_factor is 0 and the fake advances only when called; timestep_ms 50 is the declared physics/control interval (env dt 0.05, SDF max_step_size 0.050, dynamics --rate 20), not a measured wall-clock latency
the upstream environment exposes no get_state/set_state, so the package offers no snapshot or restore
the package declares only the fake backend; a live run needs Docker Engine, the gdr2-image, ROS 2 Humble and Gazebo Harmonic as the README describes, none of which the gate contacts
observations are Python floats and lists; upstream returns float32 numpy arrays with the same position and velocity values
the fake's start state and reset draws are test data, not calibrated against a live dynamics node

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: An e-stop freezes the simulated world in software: no step is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the last observation and tick stay readable; this is a simulation latch, not a physical stop.
